data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Popper's preference for better-corroborated theories is defensible on his own terms not as an inductive inference of future success, but as a non-inductive methodological rule grounded in 'verisimilitude' (truth-likeness) and the logical asymmetry of testing: while corroboration reports past performance without predicting the future, choosing the theory with higher verisimilitude is the only rational strategy for problem-solving that accepts the risk of error without violating the prohibition on induction.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If verisimilitude cannot be estimated without inductive assumptions about the uniformity of nature.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If Popper's rejection of evolutionary epistemology undermines the pragmatic argument for preferring survived theories.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the distinction between psychological habit and rational justification collapses when the agent must 'act' on the theory.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the preference for high-content theories implicitly assumes that nature is simple or regular.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The mechanism distinguishes between 'corroboration' (a historical report of severe testing survival) and 'verisimilitude' (a logical estimate of closeness to truth). The preference is justified pragmatically: if we must act, we choose the theory that has withstood more severe tests because it logically contains more empirical content and has survived attempts to falsify it, making it the best available approximation of truth, even though this offers no guarantee (induction) that it will survive the next test. This avoids smuggling in induction by treating the choice as a critical decision rather than a probabilistic prediction.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
